summary: TerraMatch is an interactive 3-D globe (plus a 2-D map) that finds the best Earth analogs for permanent Moon base locations. For 30 Moon targets (the 20 Artemis III south-pole landing and ice zones, plus 10 target tiles including the Mare Tranquillitatis lava-tube pit) it scores 4,310 Earth tiles of 10 x 10 km: 30 named analog sites, 190 impact structures, 1,091 volcanoes and about 3,000 barren and polar samples. Each place is scored in 9 categories (terrain, geology, temperature, illumination, water/ice, dust, biological sterility, caves, operations) from NASA LRO (LOLA, Diviner), USGS lunar geology, Copernicus DEM, MODIS, NASA POWER and JAXA data, with a fine-tuned geology language model. It then gives a verdict for 14 field-test experiments (rover mobility, ice prospecting, ISRU, dust mitigation, cave robotics, EVA geology training and more) with an honest list of what each site cannot reproduce. No place on Earth reproduces the lunar south pole, so TerraMatch shows which aspect each site matches, helping mission teams choose the right analog for each test and discover new, less-characterized candidates.
details:
What it does

Pick a Moon target on the 3-D globe and TerraMatch colours every Earth place by how closely it matches, shows a verdict badge (sufficient / partial / avoid) and opens a Similarity Assessment for any place: score per category, verdict per field-test experiment, and an "also account for" list of what the site cannot reproduce. Live site: https://talmzr.github.io/Earth-analog-finder/ (2-D map at /map.html). Code: https://github.com/Talmzr/Earth-analog-finder

  • 30 Moon targets: 20 Artemis III landing and ice zones (10 regions x 2) and 10 target tiles, including the Tranquillitatis pit (lava-tube skylight).
  • 4,310 Earth tiles (10 x 10 km): 30 named analog sites, 190 impact structures, 1,091 volcanoes and about 3,000 random barren and polar samples, so new analogs can be found, not only known ones.
  • 9 categories scored from -1 to +1: terrain, geology, temperature, illumination, water/ice, dust/regolith, biological sterility, caves, operations.
  • 14 experiments: landing hazard detection, rover mobility, ice prospecting, ISRU, dust mitigation, cave robotics, EVA geology training, habitat operations, planetary protection and others.

How it works

  • Terrain: relief, slope, roughness and share of steep ground measured on LOLA 80 m (Moon) vs Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (Earth).
  • Geology: USGS Unified Geologic Map of the Moon unit text vs Macrostrat bedrock text, compared with a BGE-small text model fine-tuned contrastively on Moon/Earth lithology pairs, plus a rock-type match (e.g. anorthosite).
  • Illumination: noon sun height and share of grazing sun in the Earth "light-twin month" vs LOLA average solar visibility (including crater shadows).
  • Temperature and ice: Diviner polar and global products (temperatures, cold traps, ice stability depth) vs NASA POWER, MODIS LST and ESA CCI permafrost.
  • Dust and sterility: MODIS bare ground and vegetation, volcanic tephra, rainfall (NASA POWER, JAXA GSMaP).
  • Operations: terrain match, slope hazard, open bare ground and freedom from forest, towns, water and crops (ESA WorldCover, MODIS land cover).
  • Category scores are calibrated against 161 draft anchor labels (site-grouped 5-fold cross-validation). The overall score is an experiment-weighted mean of the site-specific categories with a ground-cover gate. Each experiment is "sufficient" when every required category meets its minimum, "avoid" only when one is clearly misleading.

Results and validation

  • Category error 0.137 on the -1..+1 scale vs 0.474 for a naive baseline (cross-validated).
  • Known polar analogs (Dry Valleys, Beacon Valley, Haughton, Svalbard) rank above the other named sites with AUC 0.939.
  • Real analog campaigns (Desert RATS, RESOLVE, PANGAEA, BRAILLE, FINESSE, Apollo geology training, CanMoon) are not rated "avoid" for 85% (dev) and 97% (held-out) of their Moon targets.
  • Top picks: for the Artemis III south-pole regions, ice-free Antarctica (McMurdo Dry Valleys, Royal Society Range, Dronning Maud Land nunataks) and High Arctic polar deserts lead; for geology, anorthosite sites such as Mistastin; for the Tranquillitatis pit, young basaltic lava-tube fields such as Harrat Kishb and Afar.

Benefits and impact

Mission teams and researchers can choose the right analog for each specific test instead of one "Moon-like" site, see the caveats up front (gravity, vacuum, radiation and 25-110 K permanent shadow can never be reproduced on Earth), and discover new, less-characterized candidate sites around the world. Everything uses open data and runs on a laptop CPU in about one minute.

Tools

Python (pandas, numpy, rasterio, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers), fine-tuned BAAI bge-small-en-v1.5 (geology) and Meta DINOv2-small (terrain, evaluated), Google Colab T4 GPU for training, HTML/JavaScript 3-D globe and 2-D map hosted on GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions.

Limits

Anchor labels are drafts awaiting expert review; Earth climate layers are coarser (5-50 km) than the tiles; Antarctica lacks some land-cover, soil and bedrock layers, so fallbacks are used there.
